title: Prenatal exposure to perfluorinated chemicals and behavioral or coordination problems at age 7 years.
ehr_evidence: We used data from the Danish National Birth Cohort, which enrolled mothers in early pregnancy, and we measured maternal blood levels of PFOA and PFOS using specimens drawn around 8 weeks of gestation.
summary: Prospective birth cohort study investigating whether prenatal exposure to PFOA and PFOS is associated with behavioral or coordination problems in children at age 7.
key_findings: No significant association between maternal PFOA or PFOS levels and behavioral problems (SDQ total difficulties OR=0.91, 95% CI: 0.43–1.92 for highest vs lowest PFOA quartile) or motor coordination disorders (DCD OR=1.14, 95% CI: 0.46–2.81).

Inverse associations were observed for some PFOA quartiles with emotional symptoms (OR=0.48, 95% CI: 0.24–0.97) and hyperactivity (OR=0.51, 95% CI: 0.28–0.94), but overall background levels were not associated with neurodevelopmental problems.
captured_features: maternal plasma PFOA and PFOS concentrations
population: children aged 7 years from the Danish National Birth Cohort (n=787 for behavioral outcomes, n=537 for coordination outcomes)
limitations: selection bias due to higher socioeconomic status and healthier characteristics of participating mothers
loss to follow-up with approximately 35% not completing the 7-year interview
reliance on parent-reported questionnaires for outcomes
background exposure levels may not reflect high-dose effects observed in animal studies
